info.title: Prairie Connect API
info.description:
API for the Prairie Connect rail logistics platform — directory/marketplace,
universal search, corridor atlas, route finder, and the AI guide.

**Auth**: integrate directly with the Cognito User Pool (Amplify Auth or
amazon-cognito-identity-js) and send the resulting JWT as a Bearer token.

**Realtime**: fetch `/v1/realtime/token` for the MQTT-over-WSS config;
chat replies stream there as `{type: delta|action|done}` events.

**Chatbot UI actions**: assistant replies carry an `actions` array (see the
`UiAction` schema) the client should execute — show a map, navigate, draw a
route, open directory results.

bearerAuth.description: Cognito JWT (id or access token). Sign in against the Cognito User Pool (see stack outputs userPoolId / userPoolClientId) and paste the token here.

slug.description: Derived from the name when omitted

railLineId.description: Build the corridor around this rail line: geometry is copied from it and its rail graph is tagged with the corridor

slug.description: Derived from the name when omitted

railLineId.description: Set to relink (geometry is re-copied) or null to detach

logoUrl.description: Public URL when a logo is set

edgeCount.description: Routing graph edges derived from this line

segmentCount.description: LineStrings found in the source GeoJSON

slug.description: Derived from the name when omitted

geojson.description: GeoJSON FeatureCollection, Feature, LineString, or MultiLineString (object or JSON string). Non-line features are ignored.

buildGraph.description: Also derive rail_nodes / rail_edges for the routing engine

snapToleranceM.description: Segment endpoints within this distance (metres) of an existing node reuse it — stitches lines into one routable network

geojson.description: Replace geometry from GeoJSON; clears and rebuilds the derived routing graph by default

rebuildGraph.description: When geojson is provided, rebuild rail_nodes / rail_edges

key.description: S3 key — send back in PATCH after PUT succeeds

logoUrl.description: Public URL the logo will be served from

geometry.description: GeoJSON FeatureCollection of the route edges

reverse.description: Reverse routing (site -> markets) uses reverse cost weights

geometry.description: GeoJSON FeatureCollection of every leg; features carry a `mode` property (truck | rail edge modes)

actions.description: UI actions for the client to execute (show a map, navigate, draw a route...). Also streamed live on the conversation's realtime topic.

path.description: App-relative path to send the user to, e.g. '/directory', '/route-finder', '/corridors/great-western'

filter.description: Filter to apply to the directory view

routeId.description: A saved route id to display, if one exists

conversationId.description: Omit to start a new conversation

key.description: S3 key the file will live at

url.description: Presigned PUT URL — upload the file body here

allOf.description: The ingestion job if one was started (null when ingest=false)

type.description: e.g. intent_selected, search_performed, listing_viewed, corridor_viewed, route_generated, partner_card_clicked, contact_button_clicked, ai_prompt_used, document_downloaded

post.description: Creates a listing in `pending` status. Admins move it to `published` after verification.

get.summary: Get one listing by id or slug

patch.description: Owners can edit their own listings; only admins can change `status` or `verified`.

get.description: Full-text + fuzzy search over published directory listings, with optional sector and geo-radius filters. `mode=semantic` uses vector similarity; `mode=hybrid` fuses both rankings.
All corridors (18 short lines + CN & CPKC), without geometry. Fetch a single corridor for its GeoJSON.

409.description: Corridor is referenced by other records

post.description: Pass `railLineId` to build the corridor around an imported rail line: its geometry is copied onto the corridor and its routing graph is tagged with the corridor. Operator defaults to the rail line's operator.

200.description: All imported rail lines with graph stats

post.summary: Import a rail line from GeoJSON
post.description: Stores the line geometry and (by default) derives the pgRouting graph: one edge per source LineString, endpoints snapped onto existing nodes so separately imported lines stitch into one routable network.

get.summary: Get a rail line with geometry (admin)

200.description: Rail line detail incl. GeoJSON geometry

patch.description: Edit metadata (name, slug, operator, description). Optionally replace geometry from GeoJSON, which clears and rebuilds the derived routing graph and syncs linked corridors.

delete.summary: Delete a rail line and its derived graph
delete.description: Removes the line, its edges, and nodes not shared with other lines. Corridors built on it keep their copied geometry but lose the link.

post.summary: Get a presigned URL to upload a rail line logo
post.description: Returns a presigned PUT URL for the public assets bucket. Upload the image bytes directly (same Content-Type), then PATCH the rail line with the returned `key` as `logoKey`.

patch.summary: Attach an uploaded logo to a rail line

200.description: One page of users, newest first

post.summary: Find a route across the rail network
post.description: Snaps origin/destination to the nearest rail nodes and runs pgRouting (Dijkstra) over the network graph. Returns ordered segments plus a GeoJSON FeatureCollection for the map.

404.description: No route found (empty network or disconnected nodes)

post.description: Prototype of the truck → transload → rail → transload/port → truck flow: trucks the load to the nearest rail-served directory site, routes it across the rail network with pgRouting, then trucks the final leg. Truck legs are straight-line estimates with a road-circuity factor.

404.description: No rail-served sites with locations, or no rail path between them

post.summary: Send a message to the assistant
post.description: Runs one assistant turn. The reply streams live on the conversation's realtime topic (`<prefix>/user/<sub>/chat/<conversationId>` — deltas, then actions, then done); the full reply and validated UI actions are also returned here. Omit `conversationId` to start a new conversation.

200.description: The assistant's reply and UI actions

get.description: Returns everything needed to open the MQTT-over-WSS connection: connect to `wss://<endpoint>/mqtt?x-amz-customauthorizer-name=<authorizer>` passing your Cognito JWT as the MQTT password (any username). Subscribe to the topics returned — the authorizer scopes you to your own subtree.

post.description: Stores authored text as a markdown document in the corpus. Call the sync endpoint afterward (or batch several adds, then sync once) to ingest it into the vector store.

201.description: Stored; key in the corpus bucket

post.summary: Get a presigned upload URL for a file
post.description: Returns a presigned PUT URL. Upload the file bytes directly to it (PDF, docx, txt, md). Then call the sync endpoint to ingest. The same Content-Type must be sent on the PUT.

schema.description: Filter by key prefix, e.g. 'knowledge/' or 'uploads/'

parameters.description: Filter by key prefix, e.g. 'knowledge/' or 'uploads/'
parameters.name: prefix

delete.description: Removes the object (and its metadata sidecar). Run a sync afterward so the vector store drops the chunks.

post.description: Triggers a Bedrock ingestion job that (re)chunks and embeds the corpus into the Aurora vector store. Returns the job id to poll. Returns 409 if the Knowledge Base isn't configured yet.

post.summary: Export platform data into the knowledge corpus
post.description: Mirrors live platform content — all corridors and published directory listings — into the corpus as markdown documents (under `platform/`), removing docs for entities that no longer qualify. By default also starts an ingestion job so the chatbot picks up the changes; pass `?ingest=false` to export only.

schema.description: Start a Bedrock ingestion job after exporting

parameters.description: Start a Bedrock ingestion job after exporting
parameters.name: ingest

get.description: The curated "I want to..." pathways for the home screen. Each carries default filters, suggested search terms, a destination page, CTA buttons, and AI starter prompts — so basic navigation never needs an AI call.

get.summary: Get a pathway with resolved content
get.description: Everything needed to render a pathway page: copy, guided questions, CTAs, AI starter prompts, plus resolved related corridors, related listings, curated routes, and featured placements targeted at this intent.

Premium listings, corridor sponsors, and featured partners targeted at the current context. All filters are optional; placements that don't target a dimension match any value for it. Results are ordered by weight.

Examples: `?page=search&sector=agrivalue&region=sk`, `?corridor=gwr`, `?intent=move-goods-by-rail`, `?listingType=transload`.

schema.description: UI surface: home | search | directory | corridor | intent | listing | route-finder | map

parameters.description: UI surface: home | search | directory | corridor | intent | listing | route-finder | map
parameters.name: page

schema.description: Province code: bc | ab | sk | mb

parameters.description: Province code: bc | ab | sk | mb
parameters.name: region

post.description: Inquiry capture for every "contact this railway / transload / ask about this route / request an opportunity pack" action. No auth required — anonymous visitors can submit; if a Bearer token is present the lead is attributed to that user.

Lightweight, batched event ingest (1-50 events per call). The event vocabulary is open — suggested types: intent_selected, search_performed, listing_viewed, corridor_viewed, route_generated, partner_card_clicked, contact_button_clicked, ai_prompt_used, document_downloaded. Send a client-generated sessionId to stitch funnels. No auth required; signed-in users are attributed automatically.

get.description: The registry of map layers the UI can render — short lines, Class I connections, interchanges, ports, transloads, communities, development sites, resource clusters, route segments, featured partners. Layers report "available" or "planned" so the frontend stays config-driven and picks up new layers without code changes. `source.hint` says where to fetch the data today.
